reasons: Directionally wrong for our side: the rationale itself confirms the Agreement contains no audit, inspection or verification right against Customer, yet the redline affirmatively grants Kubient a new verification right. AUDIT is a constraining rule on a vendor right; where that right is absent, the customer is already better off than the preferred position and no edit is warranted.

The premise that 'silence is not protection' is not supportable — absent an express grant, Kubient has no contractual basis to demand audits or system access, so the walk-away risk (unlimited/unannounced audits, remote access) is not live. Creating the right and then bounding it hands the counterparty leverage it did not have.
Correct handling is to record this as compliant/not-applicable internal evidence (no redline, no counterparty comment), not as a 'missing' deviation requiring an insertion.
The comment invites negotiation on notice period and cost-shift threshold for an audit right the counterparty never asked for, which risks anchoring a worse outcome than the current silence.

Deterministic checks passing (frequency limited, operation applies) only confirm the inserted text matches the parameter template; they do not cure the fact that the insertion is adverse to the party we represent.
